subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these could cause a species to become extinct?
options: A new predator or disease and loss of habitat
questions.explain: New predators, disease, habitat destruction or environmental change can all drive a species to extinction.

questions.q: One disadvantage of selective breeding is that it:
options: Can reduce genetic variation, increasing the risk of disease
questions.explain: Selective breeding reduces variation (inbreeding), making organisms more vulnerable to disease.

questions.q: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria such as MRSA are a problem because:
options: They reproduce too slowly to spread
Existing antibiotics no longer kill them, so infections are hard to treat
They are killed instantly by all antibiotics
questions.explain: Resistant bacteria survive treatment, making infections difficult to cure and able to spread between people.

questions.q: A heterozygous brown-eyed parent (Bb) and a blue-eyed parent (bb) have children, where brown (B) is dominant. What ratio of brown to blue eyes is expected?
questions.explain: A Bb x bb cross gives Bb and bb offspring in equal numbers, a 1:1 ratio of brown to blue eyes.

questions.q: Bacteria can be genetically engineered to produce human insulin. The human insulin gene is:
options: Cut out and inserted into the bacterium's DNA so it makes insulin
Changed into a bacterial gene by sunlight
questions.explain: The insulin gene is cut out and inserted into bacterial DNA, so the bacteria produce human insulin.

questions.q: Which is a real example of genetic engineering?
options: Bacteria modified to produce human insulin
Dogs bred for a calm temperament
questions.explain: Bacteria can be genetically modified to make human insulin, used to treat diabetes.

questions.q: Which pair of sex chromosomes is found in a typical human male?
questions.explain: Human males have XY sex chromosomes, while females have XX.

questions.q: Selective breeding for desirable traits over many generations can cause problems because reduced variation may lead to:
options: Inbreeding, making the population vulnerable to disease or genetic defects
questions.explain: Selective breeding reduces the gene pool, so a single disease or defect can affect many individuals (inbreeding).

questions.q: Studying the genome (DNA) of organisms has improved classification because it:
options: Proves that all species are identical
Replaces the need for naming organisms
Shows how closely related species are by comparing their DNA
questions.explain: Comparing DNA reveals evolutionary relationships, leading to changes such as the three-domain classification system.

questions.q: A farmer breeds the cows that produce the most milk together over many generations. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Choosing parents with a desired trait (high milk yield) to breed together over generations is selective breeding.

questions.q: How does meiosis differ from mitosis?
options: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and makes varied gametes; mitosis makes identical diploid cells
Mitosis makes gametes; meiosis makes body cells
questions.explain: Meiosis halves chromosome number to form varied gametes, whereas mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.

questions.q: Identical twins have the same genes but can still show small differences. These differences are caused by:
questions.explain: Identical twins share the same genotype, so any differences between them are due to environmental factors.

questions.q: Sickle cell disease is an inherited disorder caused by a recessive allele. A person who is a carrier:
options: Has one allele for it but does not show the disease, and can pass it on
Always shows symptoms of the disease
Has the disease but cannot pass it on
questions.explain: A carrier is heterozygous: they carry one recessive allele without showing the disorder but can pass it to offspring.

questions.q: DNA is described as a polymer with what overall shape?
questions.explain: DNA is a double helix, two strands twisted together, made of repeating nucleotide units (a polymer).

questions.q: Which of these is an example of variation caused mostly by the environment?
questions.explain: A scar is an environmental (acquired) variation, not caused by genes.

questions.q: The rapid emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is evidence for evolution because:
options: Resistant bacteria survive antibiotics and reproduce, so resistance spreads
Antibiotics create resistant bacteria from nothing
questions.explain: Resistant bacteria survive and reproduce by natural selection, demonstrating evolution happening quickly.

questions.q: What determines whether a human baby is biologically male or female?
options: Whether the sperm carries an X or Y chromosome
Whether the egg carries an X or Y chromosome
questions.explain: Eggs always carry X; the sperm carries either X (giving XX, female) or Y (giving XY, male), so the sperm determines sex.

questions.q: How can the development of antibiotic resistance be slowed down?
options: Not finishing the full course of antibiotics
Only prescribing antibiotics when needed and finishing the full course
questions.explain: Reducing unnecessary use and always completing the course helps stop resistant bacteria surviving and spreading.

questions.q: Selective breeding (artificial selection) involves:
options: Letting nature choose which organisms survive
Humans choosing organisms with desired traits to breed together
questions.explain: In selective breeding humans choose parents with desirable characteristics to breed over many generations.

questions.q: Why did it take a long time for Darwin's theory to be widely accepted?
options: No one was interested in biology
It conflicted with religious beliefs and the mechanism of inheritance was not yet known
questions.explain: Darwin's theory challenged religious views and lacked a known mechanism of inheritance (genes were not yet understood).

questions.q: Gametes (sex cells) such as sperm and egg are described as haploid because they contain:
options: Half the normal number of chromosomes (23 in humans)
Twice the normal number of chromosomes
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid, carrying a single set of chromosomes (23 in humans) so the full number is restored at fertilisation.

questions.q: A herd of giraffes lives where food is high in the trees. Over many generations, longer necks become common. The best explanation is that:
options: Giraffes stretched their necks and passed this on
Giraffes with longer necks survived better and reproduced, passing on the alleles
The trees caused the necks to grow
All giraffes decided to grow longer necks
questions.explain: Natural selection: giraffes with naturally longer necks reached more food, survived and passed on those alleles.
